description: We are a passionate and creative team of space enthusiasts, innovators, and problem-solvers united by our curiosity about space and technology. Our goal is to transform ideas into meaningful solutions by combining creativity, scientific thinking, and technology. Through the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we aim to explore real-world challenges, develop innovative solutions, and contribute to a better understanding of our universe. We believe in teamwork, learning, and pushing the boundaries
summary:
**Lunar Survival** is an interactive Moon exploration and survival game developed in Unreal Engine. Players become an astronaut establishing a lunar outpost, managing oxygen, water, food and power while exploring with a rover. They build solar equipment that tracks the Sun, grow food, collect lunar samples and complete science missions.

The project addresses the **Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer** challenge by turning astronaut preparation into hands-on learning. Guided objectives, visual resource indicators and contextual help introduce life-support management, energy planning and exploration safety. Simulated solar events, impacts, moonquakes and cold conditions encourage players to recognize hazards and make decisions about supplies and shelter.

Using NASA resources and models alongside simplified educational scenarios, the game connects space science with understandable gameplay. It matters because interactive experiences can make the challenges of living beyond Earth more accessible, helping young learners develop curiosity, problem-solving skills and an appreciation for the planning behind human space exploration.
details:
What does the project do?

Lunar Survival is a single-player Moon exploration and survival game. Players establish an outpost, explore with a rover, collect samples and complete science missions while managing oxygen, water, food, health and power.

The base connects these systems: solar panels track the Sun to generate electricity, life-support equipment supplies oxygen, and plants need water before producing food. Players prepare supplies before travelling, use tools for field tasks and seek shelter during simulated hazards. A contextual tutorial, compass and quest-help system explain what to do without overwhelming players with text.

How does it address the challenge?

The project supports the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge by turning mission preparation into practical decisions. Players learn to check supplies, plan journeys, maintain equipment and respond to changing conditions. Actions have consequences: travelling without enough oxygen or neglecting power makes exploration harder.

NASA resources, terrain data and spacecraft models connect the experience to space science. Survival values and hazard timing are simplified for learning and gameplay; the project is not a scientific mission simulator.

Benefits and intended impact

The intended impact is to make astronaut preparation accessible and engaging, especially for younger learners. The game encourages curiosity, resource planning and problem-solving through experimentation. Its visual interface helps players understand relationships between energy, life support, food production and exploration.

Tools and technology

  • Unreal Engine 5.8 for gameplay, rendering, lighting and packaging.
  • Blueprint visual scripting for survival systems, missions, interactions, menus and audio scheduling.
  • Python and Unreal’s editor scripting tools for asset processing, development automation and verification.
  • Blender for preparing, resizing and optimizing models.
  • NASA resources and user-supplied models for parts of the environment and equipment.
  • Microsoft C++ Build Tools and Windows SDK for producing the Windows Shipping build.

The exported game runs on a Windows PC. Development considered hardware constraints through graphics presets, bounded visual-effect pools, texture and audio budgets, and compressed packaging.

What makes it creative?

The project combines exploration, base maintenance and astronaut training in one connected experience. Sun-tracking solar equipment, a greenhouse food loop, interactive field tools and a drivable rover give learning objectives a physical role in the world. Context-sensitive calm and danger soundtracks reinforce the player’s situation.

Factors considered

Development balanced educational clarity, visual realism, accessibility, performance and playability. The interface uses icons, bars and nearby prompts; optional help supports beginners. Hazards include warnings and shelter opportunities, while gameplay systems remain simplified enough to understand through play.
